about.title: West Covina Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Nearly every product in a West Covina home passed through several hands before it reached you: the company that designed it, the plant that built it, the distributor that shipped it, and the store along Azusa Avenue or Amar Road where you bought it. When that product fails and someone is hurt, California law lets you look at the whole chain. Product liability claims usually rest on strict liability, so you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a defect — in its design, in how your particular unit was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. Examples here vary widely: a tire that separates on the I-10, a space heater that ignites, a car seat latch that gives way, a medication whose label omitted a serious risk. Whatever the product, keep it. Do not repair it, return it, or throw it away. LawProactive is not a law firm; we connect you, free, with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why West Covina Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Attorneys who know strict liability
items.desc: Under California law you usually do not have to prove a company was negligent — only that the product was defective and that the defect hurt you. The independent attorneys in our network build cases around that standard.

items.title: Guidance on preserving the product
items.desc: The product itself is often the single most important piece of evidence. An attorney can help you secure it, along with receipts, packaging, and photos, before anyone asks you to send it back.

items.title: Every link in the supply chain is examined
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all share responsibility for a defective product in California. Your attorney can identify each party rather than settling for the first name on the box.

items.question: My tire blew out on the I-10 through West Covina. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. If the tire separated because of a manufacturing or design defect, you may have a strict liability claim against the tire maker and the shop that sold it, separate from any claim against another driver. Keep the tire, the wheel, and your service records rather than letting a tow yard dispose of them. An attorney can arrange for an inspection to determine what actually failed.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer did something wrong?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, which means the focus is on the product, not the company's behavior. You need to show a defect in design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. That is a very different burden than proving someone was careless.

items.question: I bought the item at a store in West Covina, but the manufacturer is overseas. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Yes. California law allows claims against distributors and retailers as well as manufacturers, so the local store that sold you the product may be a responsible party even if the maker is hard to reach. This is one reason to hold on to your receipt or order confirmation. An independent attorney can sort out which parties to pursue.
